title: Receipt-authenticated lazy Wasm modules
objective: Separate precompiled lazy Python templates from compiler-worker stdlib transport and load their authenticated bundle directly in the evaluator before synchronous imports

oracles: deterministic resolver/receipt fixtures and existing flint-wasm build contract

handoff.summary: Separated 172 precompiled lazy Python templates from stdlib/compiler-worker transport into a strict evaluator-owned sagejs.lazy-module-bundle/v1 asset. The evaluator fetches the bundle in parallel, validates canonical names, source digests, virtual filenames, package paths, and templates before installing a synchronous loader, while transactional host cleanup restores every temporary global. A packaging checkpoint copies the 26,194,522-byte bundle byte-for-byte, authenticates its SHA-256 87d3312c4bd256525f57bb734dc61868484401f923309c779c1aa0b255378e32 in checkpoint identity sha256:2a44116997785ebeb795ac4d4335c3073451a1586f96dfa57ba6d337917b5a16, and binds the generator, config, and every referenced Python source into the receipt closure. stdlib.json contains no lazyModules member, so approximately 25 MiB is no longer parsed or structured-cloned through the compiler worker.
risks: The full Chromium smoke initialized the evaluator and synchronously imported math, then hit an unrelated stale expected rendering of 1 instead of the current correct float rendering 1.0.
The broad unit tier in this isolated worktree requires a separately generated dist/module-cache canonical cache; its focused provenance, receipt, loader, and evaluator lifecycle tests all pass.
next_steps: Register test/lazy-module-provenance.cjs in the shared unit test manifest as coordinated with the root integration lane.

After the pending FFI resource and dynamic-execution commits integrate, rebase exact root and regenerate the ignored final production bundle and receipt so build-receipt.source.gitCommit records the release commit, then run all release workflows.
